hedge_exemplars.value: If measured thermal storage in urban fabric is insufficient to account for the observed nocturnal temperature surplus
If anthropogenic heat emissions (e.g., traffic, HVAC) are negligible, the radiative budget alone may be insufficient to explain the observed temperature gap.
If the nocturnal UHI is observed to be stronger in cities with low building density and high sky view factor, this mechanism is insufficient.
If heavily irrigated, vegetated cities still exhibit a large nocturnal UHI, the evapotranspiration mechanism is insufficient.
If rural areas with equally low sky view factors (e.g., forests) do not exhibit comparable nighttime warmth, the mechanism is insufficient.
If anthropogenic heat output is measured to be a small fraction of the total energy balance surplus, the mechanism is insufficient.
If thermal mass is shown to dominate over emissivity in predicting cooling rates, this mechanism is insufficient.
If measured turbulent sensible heat flux out of the urban canopy is not suppressed relative to rural areas, the mechanism is insufficient.
